key_insight: This review maps medical vision-language foundation models, from contrastive alignment and generative systems to pixel grounding, mixture-of-experts, and reinforcement-learning-based reasoning.
clinical_relevance: Aligning medical images with clinical text could support image interpretation, report generation, and question answering while reducing reliance on manual annotations.
method: Reviews foundation models that learn from paired medical images and text.
Organizes architectures into a medical vision-language model taxonomy.
Examines data, reliability, computation, and evaluation challenges.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports no quantitative performance results and highlights limited data and a lack of standardized, clinically grounded evaluation metrics.
watch_item: Hallucinated diagnostic content remains a risk; the review does not establish safety or effectiveness for clinical deployment.
paper_title: Multimodal AI in Healthcare: Review of Vision-Language Foundation Models for Real-World Medical Applications
